title: Trump Said Very Weak. Satellite Shows the Al Udeid Radome Is a Blackened Smear. The Pentagon Only Overseas Secure Comms Node Is Gone.
narrative:
Iran launched a retaliatory missile attack on Al Udeid Air Base in Qatar on June 23, 2025, following US strikes on three Iranian nuclear facilities. President Trump immediately dismissed the attack as very weak, posting on Truth Social that 13 missiles were knocked down and 1 was set free and that hardly any damage was done. Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell told Iran International that the impact did minimal damage to equipment and structures on the base and that Al Udeid Air Base remains fully operational. CENTCOM initial statement described the attack as successfully defended against by US and Qatari air defense systems.

Satellite imagery obtained by Iran International from US geospatial analytics company Satellogic, captured June 24, one day after the attack, tells a different story. The imagery shows the base distinctive white geodesic radome, which housed the 15 million Modernized Enterprise Terminal (MET), reduced to what Iran International describes as a blackened smear. The MET was the first such terminal installed outside the United States, providing secure voice, video, and data communications linking service members in CENTCOM area of responsibility with military leaders worldwide. A 2016 US Air Force press release described it featuring anti-jamming technology.

The Pentagon characterization of minimal damage and fully operational is technically defensible only if the MET destruction is excluded from the assessment. The satellite image shows no apparent damage elsewhere on the sprawling base, meaning the Iranian missile appears to have achieved a precision strike on the single most strategically valuable communications node at the facility. Defense analyst Farzin Nadimi of the Washington Institute noted that US Army Patriot systems and Qatari systems had just about two minutes to respond from detection, and suggested an Iranian drone may have slipped through while batteries were engaged with incoming missiles.
analysis:
The destruction of the MET creates a specific operational gap: CENTCOM forward headquarters lost its primary secure communications hub, the only one of its kind deployed overseas. The Pentagon has not disclosed whether the MET has been replaced or whether temporary communications alternatives are in use. This is the same pattern seen at Ali Al Salem and other Gulf bases, official statements characterize damage as minimal while satellite evidence reveals precision destruction of high-value nodes.

The very weak characterization versus the blackened-smear satellite image is a clean, falsifiable contradiction. The MET destruction is strategically significant precisely because it was the only one outside the US, its loss degrades CENTCOM secure communications architecture in the theater where the US just fought a 12-day war. The Pentagon minimal damage framing is technically true if you count runways and taxiways, but false if you count the communications node that makes the base the nerve center of US Middle East military operations.

The pattern at Al Udeid mirrors the Ali Al Salem ASR-1000 radar destruction, the Ahmad Al Jaber FPS radar hit, and the Fifth Fleet SATCOM terminal loss, all cases where a single precision-guided munition achieved a strategically disproportionate effect against a high-value node, and all cases where official damage assessments either excluded the specific node or characterized the loss as minimal. Iran missile accuracy against fixed communications and radar installations appears to have been consistently underestimated across the entire Gulf theater.
verdict: [SIPHONED VERDICT]: Trump very weak characterization of the Al Udeid strike is contradicted by Satellogic imagery showing the 15M MET radome, CENTCOM only overseas secure communications terminal, reduced to a blackened smear. The Pentagon fully operational claim is technically true only if you exclude the single most strategically valuable node on the base. Has the MET been replaced? If not, CENTCOM is operating on backup communications in the theater where it may need to strike Iran again.
